Thought: To solve this problem, I need to consider the properties of sodium chloride and iodine, as well as the separation techniques listed in the options. Sodium chloride (NaCl) is a solid ionic compound that does not sublimate, whereas iodine is a solid that can sublimate, meaning it can transition from solid to gas without going through a liquid phase. 

Given this property, sublimation can be used to separate iodine from sodium chloride. When the mixture is heated, iodine will sublimate, leaving behind sodium chloride. None of the other techniques are as suitable for this specific separation, as they do not take advantage of the sublimation property of iodine.
